A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CyclicReflex research, with matching authors, central equations, experiments, and generation examples. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite substantial additions and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, decoding comparisons, self-correction tests, search-integration experiments, and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds science and coding evaluations, Qwen3 results, Pass@N experiments, and scheduling and token-set comparisons.

M1.justification: The triangular logit schedule in Equation (3) is unchanged. However, Appendix B introduces an optional dynamic reflection-token variant that expands its token set during decoding using token ranks and a logit-gap condition. This changes an auxiliary procedure without replacing the central method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates mathematical reasoning on MATH500, AIME2024/2025, and AMC2023. v2 retains these and adds GPQA Diamond science questions and LiveCodeBench coding evaluation, substantially broadening the represented domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: The Silver baseline evaluated across three models and four benchmarks in v1 Table 4 disappears. v2 Table A3 adds random-adjustment and linear-decay comparators and evaluates positive-adjustment TIP across all four math benchmarks. Positive TIP was already explored on MATH500 in v1 Figure 2, so that component is extended rather than wholly new.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-4B/8B/14B configurations and Pass@N evaluation at N = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Difficulty comparisons replace the motivating alpha sweep and added-correct-answer displays with absolute accuracies. Existing decoding defaults remain unchanged. Appendix B also revises the stated sensitivity metric and amplitudes, but these conflict with the retained heatmap and do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds fixed-versus-dynamic token-set robustness tests, alternative scheduling controls, reflection-token position distributions, and Pass@N scaling analysis. It removes the original motivating alpha sweep and the reflection-count and generation-length sensitivity heatmaps. The self-correction, search-integration, thought-landscape, and appendix generation-example analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five re-answers per prompt condition and average accuracy for the same 50-problem self-correction experiment. Neither adds random-seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new Pass@N experiment changes sampling-budget evaluation rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All 96 numerical entries for Original, TIP, S1, and CyclicReflex in v1 Table 4 match v2 Table 2. Nevertheless, v2 adds substantial results for new domains, Qwen3, Pass@N, and scheduling controls, while removing Silver results and two sensitivity outputs. Section 3 also changes the reported Medium-group original accuracy from 82.9% to 71%; this is a revised reported result, not evidence of a matched-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 removes the explicit mathematical definition of the Silver adjustment schedule and its 2-adic valuation explanation from v1 Section 5.1. The thought-distance definition and Equations (1)–(3) remain unchanged. Neither version supplies formal guarantees or proofs for CyclicReflex.

C1.justification: The central resource-allocation framing, optimization analogy, and cyclical-decoding contribution remain intact. The abstract broadens claimed effectiveness from mathematical benchmarks and 1.5B–8B models to science, coding, and models up to 14B, and explicitly adds a claim of no additional computation cost.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking TIP's diminishing Pass@N gains to reduced sampling diversity, explaining reflection allocation through positional patterns, and arguing robustness to token-set choice. It removes the Silver-specific interpretation and discussion of amplitude controlling output length. The theoretical limitations and broader-impact discussion are substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 removes the Silver hyperparameter-search range, gamma in (1, 2]. Hardware, vLLM usage, sampling defaults, prompts, and the code-access URL remain unchanged. Best-of-N and beam-search implementation details move from the main text to Appendix A rather than being newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on test-time scaling and selection, including SEAL, Kinetics, AlphaOne, and Every Rollout Counts, plus GPQA and LiveCodeBench sources. It removes the explicit statement that reflection-token resource allocation is largely unexplored. The overall positioning around optimization-inspired, training-free reasoning control remains stable.

P1.justification: The six-section narrative and much of the prose are retained. Local changes include rewriting the motivating TIP discussion, shortening experimental setup explanations, moving difficulty analysis to Appendix B, standardizing period notation, shortening the title, and adding an LLM-writing-assistance disclosure.

P2.justification: The preprint is extensively reformatted into an ICLR layout with changed typography, margins, headers, and figure placement. v2 adds Figures 5, 6, and 8 and Tables A1–A3, redraws the motivating and difficulty comparisons, removes Silver table rows, and reduces Figure A1 from four panels to two. Its revised Figure A1 caption incorrectly describes the retained accuracy percentages as additional-correct-answer counts.

improvement.justification: The new science/coding and Qwen3 evaluations strengthen evidence of generality, while token-set and scheduling controls better examine why the method works. The net gain is limited by removal of the Silver comparison and two sensitivity outputs, and by new reporting inconsistencies: Figure A1 retains accuracy percentages but labels them improvement counts, while its accompanying text cites amplitudes absent from the plot. These tradeoffs support a modest overall improvement rather than an unqualified substantial one.
